1. Overview

Mock Tester gives pupils English practice tests on screen, from Kindergarten to Grade 5. Each test is matched to its grade. Pupils see their results as soon as they finish.

Every test has four parts. Spelling and Grammar & punctuation make up English Skills (questions ES1, ES2…). A story (Text A) and an information text (Text B) make up Reading (questions RC1, RC2…). Each question is worth 1 mark.

There are 11 forms for each grade (A–K). Each form has its own story, information text and spelling words. The spelling words are pitched to each grade's spelling patterns, and the grammar questions are drawn at random.

These are practice tests. Scores are raw marks: the number of questions answered correctly.

2. Setting up a test

  1. Grade: choose the pupil's grade, from Kindergarten to Grade 5.
  2. Form: choose A–K, or Surprise me for a random form. Give a pupil a new form each time so they never see the same questions twice.
  3. Parts of the test: untick any part you don't want. For example, run only Spelling and Grammar for a 15-minute check. At least one part must stay on. The time limit shrinks to match.
  4. Press Start test. The timer starts now.

Teacher settings

  • Set number: keep the default (2026) so Form B on screen is the same paper as Form B from Mock Maker. Change it to get a fresh set of forms for a new term.
  • Use the time limit: untick for pupils who need extra time. The timer then counts up instead of down.

3. Running the test

  • Full screen: press the corner icon. Pupils then see only the question, with Back, Skip, Next and End test in a bar at the bottom. For reading questions, the text sits beside the question and each scrolls separately.
  • Spelling: each word is read aloud automatically: the word, a sentence, then the word again. Pupils type the word and can press Listen to hear it again. Use headphones in a shared room.
  • Kindergarten and Grade 1: pupils press Listen to hear the story or information text and each question, as when a teacher reads aloud.
  • Moving around: pupils can go back, skip a question, or tap a dot on the question map to jump to it. Orange dots are skipped questions.
  • Keyboard: A–D (or 1–4) choose an answer; ← → move between questions; Enter moves on after typing a spelling.
  • Ending: End test asks pupils to confirm and lists any unanswered questions. From Grade 2 up, the test ends by itself when time runs out.
  • If the page closes: answers are saved on that computer. Reopen the app and press Resume on the start screen.

4. Paper tests

Use Mock Maker to print the same tests. Choose the grade, how many forms, and which parts, then download the student paper and teacher pack for each form.

  • Teacher pack: it holds the spelling dictation script, the read-aloud texts for Kindergarten and Grade 1, the full answer key and a class score record.
  • Dictation: say the question number and the word, read the sentence, then say the word again. Allow time to write.
  • Matching papers: a paper and its key share a paper code. Only mark a paper with the key whose code matches.

With the same set number and the same parts switched on, an on-screen form and a printed form with the same letter are the same paper. Some pupils can sit it on screen while others use paper.

5. Reading the report

The report appears as soon as the pupil ends the test. Pupils can download it as a PDF.

  • Score tiles: the percentage, correct answers, band, questions attempted, questions skipped and time taken.
  • By part: the score for Spelling, Grammar, Text A and Text B. Pupils copy these onto their score sheet.
  • Reading skills: six skills (retrieval, inference, vocabulary and language, author's technique, structure and sequence, summarising), each with a coloured bar. Green is 75% or more, orange 50–74%, red below 50%.
  • Priorities and next steps: the weakest areas, including spelling and grammar, with a teaching suggestion for each.
  • Questions to review: every missed question, the pupil's answer, the right answer and the skill it tests. Missed spellings show their spelling pattern, such as "-dge and -ge".
BandScoreWhat it suggests
Strong85% and aboveSecure at this grade; try the next grade up
Secure70–84%On track; target the weaker skills
Developing50–69%Needs focused practice in the priority skills
Needs supportBelow 50%Consider the grade below and closer support

Skill scores from small numbers of questions (for example 0 out of 2) are a prompt to look closer, not a judgement. Reading questions are tagged to skills automatically, so a few tags are debatable.

6. The score sheet

The score sheet is one page per test. Pupils record their own scores and reflect on the test. It has no bands or ratings, so the writing is the pupil's own view of how it went.

  1. Download and print: use the button on the start screen or at the end of the report. Print one per pupil for each test.
  2. Details: pupils fill in their name, class, date, grade, form and time taken.
  3. My scores for each part: pupils copy the chips at the top of the report (for example Spelling 11 / 13) and the total. They leave a row empty if that part was switched off.
  4. My scores for each reading skill: pupils copy each line of the Reading skills section, for example Inference 4 / 8.
  5. My feedback: pupils write what was hard for them in this test, and how they will work to improve before the next one.

Keep the sheets in a folder so you and the pupil can compare tests over the term. The feedback makes a good starting point for a short conference: check that the pupil's plan matches the questions in the report's review table.

7. Tips and problems

  • No sound: check the volume and headphones. Chrome and Edge have the clearest voices. If there is no audio at all, an adult can hold the button under a spelling question to see the word and read it aloud.
  • Full screen does not fill the monitor: some browsers and app views block true full screen. The app still hides everything except the question.
  • Report PDF will not download: the PDF tool needs an internet connection. The test and on-screen report work offline.
  • Results: each computer keeps its own recent results list. Results are not sent anywhere, so pupils should copy their scores onto a score sheet.
  • Classroom computers: the app works as a single HTML file. Copy it to each computer and double-click to open; no sign-in is needed.
  • Question bank: all stories, information texts, spelling words and grammar items are also kept as editable text files, so they can be checked or changed.
